title: Use of coagulation factor XIII (F13) gene as an internal control for normalization of genomic DNA’s for HLA typing
author: Neduvat, Murthy, et al.
materials: Since Qiagen columns have superior DNA properties with least PCR inhibitors [7], we used these columns for isolation of gDNA following the manufacturer’s protocols. Briefly, 200 μl of whole blood was first processed for a lysis step (RBC lysis), followed by lysis of the nucleated cells and binding of the lysed material to the column (silica membrane). After washing the column to remove the contaminants, the bound gDNA was eluted using appropriate elution buffer as recommended by the manufacturer.

steps.title: Isolate genomic DNA from blood
steps.instruction: Take 200 µL whole blood, perform RBC lysis, lyse nucleated cells, bind the lysate to a Qiagen silica‑membrane column, wash as instructed by the kit, and elute the genomic DNA with the supplied elution buffer following the manufacturer’s protocol.

substeps.instruction: Measure the concentration of the eluted gDNA with a Nanodrop spectrophotometer (A260/280 ratio recorded).

steps.title: Determine optimal annealing temperature
steps.instruction: Run a gradient PCR with the F13‑specific primers across the following temperatures: 50 °C, 51 °C, 52.9 °C, 55.7 °C, 59.1 °C, 62 °C, 63.8 °C, and 65 °C; identify the temperature range giving maximal signal (50–52.9 °C) and select the optimum annealing temperature of 51 °C for subsequent qPCR assays.

steps.title: Optimize primer concentration
steps.instruction: Test several primer concentrations; the assay yields the strongest amplification with a final primer concentration of 0.4 µM, producing a Ct of ≈7.7 and no visible primer‑dimer band.

substeps.instruction: Include a no‑template control (NTC) in each run to confirm the absence of amplification.

steps.title: Establish limit of detection
steps.instruction: Perform the F13 qPCR with template amounts down to 10 copies (≈37 attograms). The assay reliably detects 10 copies, showing the expected dose‑dependent fluorescence‑versus‑cycle curve.

steps.title: Generate F13 standard curve
steps.instruction: Prepare ten‑fold serial dilutions of the plasmid pTZ57R/T‑F13A1 covering 10⁵ to 10¹ copies per reaction. Calculate copy number using the formula: DNA (copies) = 6.022 × 10²³ × DNA amount (g) / [DNA length (bp) × 660 g mol⁻¹ bp⁻¹]. Run qPCR on these standards to obtain Ct values for the curve.

steps.title: Quantify F13 copies in samples
steps.instruction: Run the optimized F13 qPCR (51 °C annealing, 0.4 µM primers) on each isolated gDNA sample. Use the standard curve to calculate the number of F13 copies per 10 ng of genomic DNA.

steps.title: Normalize gDNA to 100 F13 copies
steps.instruction: Adjust each sample so that the amount of DNA added to downstream HLA PCR corresponds to 100 F13 copies, which is equivalent to 0.2 ng of genomic DNA.

steps.title: Perform HLA PCR on normalized DNA
steps.instruction: Using the normalized DNA (100 F13 copies per reaction), amplify HLA‑A, HLA‑B, and HLA‑C (class I) and HLA‑DPB1 exon 2, exon 3, HLA‑DRB1 exon 2, and exon 3 (class II) with the appropriate primers under the conditions described in the original method.

steps.title: Visualize PCR products by agarose gel
steps.instruction: Load the HLA PCR products onto a 1–2 % agarose gel alongside a 250 bp–10 kb DNA ladder, run electrophoresis, and compare band intensities; after normalization, bands should display nearly equal intensity across all samples.

description: The DNA sequence of one of the representative clone of pTZ57R/T-F13 is given in supplementary Fig. S1. It is evident from the DNA sequence that the amplified PCR amplicon belonged to human F13 A1 gene when analyzed and compared against the human F13A1 gene sequence available in the NCBI database. It was observed that the F13 specific primers amplified F13 gene at Tm ranging from 50 °C–59.1 °C, and the optimum activity was seen at 51 °C. (Fig. 1). F13 primers at 0.4 μM final concentration could amplify the F13 product with a Ct of 7.7 (Fig. 2) with no PD. The LOD of the F13 Q-PCR assay was found to be 10 copies (37attg), and the amplification plot of fluorescence signal versus cycle number showed the expected dose dependence curve (Fig. 3).Fig. 1Gradient PCR for F13A1 (F13) gene.Gradient PCR for F13 gene was carried out using specific primers as outlined in the M & M section.
